title: Mother-Stock Rotation and Senescence
objective: Manage mother-stock rotation using measured propagation performance, health, identity, and crop outcomes rather than folklore about clone generations.

terms.definition: Planned replacement or retirement of donor plants based on defined identity, health, propagation, and performance criteria.
Age- and development-associated decline in cellular or whole-plant function; it is not synonymous with a fixed calendar age.
Persistent change in plant performance or state over time that may arise from environment, management, development, or health without requiring a DNA-sequence change.
A change in gene regulation or chromatin state that does not require a DNA-sequence change and can persist through cell divisions.
A DNA sequence change arising after fertilization in non-germline tissue.
Verified donor or backup material maintained to replace a mother or production line when defined retirement criteria are met.

coreScience: Repeated vegetative propagation does not create Mendelian genetic drift because there is no breeding population, but clone lines can accumulate somatic variants, infections, labeling errors, and persistent physiological or epigenetic states.

Mother performance changes with root restriction, repeated pruning, nutrition, environment, disease pressure, and age. Declining cutting quality may come from management rather than irreversible genetic deterioration.

Micropropagation studies show that stability findings depend on genotype, method, passage number, and test resolution. Recent genome and methylation work supports monitoring rather than assuming indefinite stability.
cultivationRelevance: Rotate mothers when predefined evidence shows health, identity, propagation, or crop performance is unacceptable. Maintain verified backups and compare replacement candidates before retiring the only source.

measureAndRecord.requirement: Mother age and lineage; cutting cycles; rooting and rejection trends; health tests; off-types; crop performance; genetic/chemistry checks; replacement and retirement rationale.

misconceptions: Every clone generation loses a fixed percentage of vigor.
Old mothers always have mutated genetics.
Tissue culture automatically resets every problem.
evidenceLimits: Cannabis does not have a scientifically established universal maximum clone generation or mother age. Monitoring methods detect only what they measure.
